The [SHA-1 Hash Generator](/sha1-hash-generator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Generate a SHA-1 hash of any text — for checksums and legacy use. Enter your text to hash and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Generate the SHA-1 hash of any text. SHA-1 turns any input into a fixed 40-character hexadecimal fingerprint: the same input always produces the same hash, and even a one-character change produces a completely different one. It is still used to verify file checksums and in older systems such as Git, but it is broken for security — researchers can create two different inputs with the same SHA-1 hash, so never use it for passwords or security. The hashing runs in your browser with the Web Crypto API — your text is never uploaded or stored.

## How to use the SHA-1 Hash Generator

Start by typing or pasting your text to hash. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Type or paste the text you want to hash.
2. The SHA-1 hash appears instantly, in hexadecimal and in Base64.
3. Copy the hash with the copy button.

## Formula

SHA-1 processes the input in 512-bit blocks through 80 rounds of mixing, and outputs a 160-bit digest shown as 40 hexadecimal characters. It is a one-way function: you cannot recover the input from the hash.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [SHA-1 Hash Generator](/sha1-hash-generator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. The SHA-1 hash of “Hello, world!” is 943a702d06f34599aee1f8da8ef9f7296031d699. Change one letter and the hash changes completely. Try the same figures in the [SHA-1 Hash Generator](/sha1-hash-generator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

The fastest way to see what the [SHA-1 Hash Generator](/sha1-hash-generator) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What a hash is for

A hash is a fingerprint: it lets you check that data has not changed without storing the data itself. Download a file, hash it, and compare with the hash the publisher lists — if they match, the file is intact. Git uses SHA-1 to identify every commit, and many download pages still list SHA-1 checksums alongside SHA-256 ones.

## Why SHA-1 is not for security

SHA-1 was standardised in 1995 and is now broken: in 2017 researchers demonstrated a practical collision, two different files with the same SHA-1 hash, and the attack has only got cheaper since. It is fine for checksums and for identifying files in systems that already use it, but for anything security-related — passwords, signatures, certificates — use SHA-256 or SHA-512 instead. Never use plain SHA-1 to store passwords; use bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2 with a salt.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- The same input always gives the same hash — use that to verify downloads.
- For security, use SHA-256 or SHA-512 — SHA-1 is broken for that purpose.
- Hashing is one-way: you cannot turn a hash back into the original text.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is SHA-1?

A hash function that turns any input into a fixed 160-bit (40 hex character) fingerprint. It is deterministic and one-way, and a tiny change in the input produces a completely different hash. Try it with your own numbers in the [SHA-1 Hash Generator](/sha1-hash-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is SHA-1 secure?

No — not any more. Practical collisions have been demonstrated since 2017, so SHA-1 must not be used for passwords, signatures or certificates. It is still fine for checksums and legacy systems. Try it with your own numbers in the [SHA-1 Hash Generator](/sha1-hash-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is the difference between SHA-1 and SHA-256?

SHA-1 produces a 40-character hash and is broken; SHA-256 produces a 64-character hash and is still trusted. Use SHA-256 for anything new. Try it with your own numbers in the [SHA-1 Hash Generator](/sha1-hash-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is my text uploaded anywhere?

No. The hashing runs in your browser with the Web Crypto API — the text never leaves your device. Try it with your own numbers in the [SHA-1 Hash Generator](/sha1-hash-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
